title: Case Study: Enabling faster specialty pharmacy coverage decisions with lab data integration
summary: As specialty pharmaceuticals have expanded across autoimmune, oncology, and chronic conditions, one PBM's priorauthorization process became increasingly difficult to administer efficiently, as therapies required more complexand clinically specific validation.
body_markdown:
### Key takeaways:


1. Automated coverage validation using real-time lab data at the point of adjudication
2. Reduced need for manual prior authorization review and post-claim follow-ups
3. Improved provider experience by minimizing documentation requests and callbacks
4. Enabled more consistent application of coverage policies using objective clinical data
5. Supported responsible management of high cost therapies requiring clinical validation


## Working together to simplify and accelerate coverage decisions


### Background


As specialty pharmaceuticals have expanded across[autoimmune, oncology, and chronic conditions](https://www.iqvia.com/insights/the-iqvia-institute/reports-and-publications/reports/global-medicine-use-trends-2026) , one PBM's prior authorization process became increasingly difficult to administer efficiently, with therapies requiring more complex and clinically specific validation.


[Specialty drugs account for over 50% of total drug spend](https://www.iqvia.com/locations/united-states/blogs/2023/07/insights-into-the-2023-us-pharmaceutical-market) despite representing a[small share of prescriptions.](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC11607209/) They also are often associated with targeted mechanisms of action and strict eligibility criteria, increasing the need for rigorous utilization management and clinical oversight. Many specialty drug therapies[require confirmation through laboratory values and clinical thresholds before approval,](https://www.pharmacytimes.com/view/a-primer-for-medical-specialty-drug-utilization-management-strategies#:~:text=lab) reflecting a broader shift toward targeted, biomarker-driven treatments and more precise eligibility criteria.


Because this coverage criteria for specialty drugs requires more than just procedure codes and diagnosis documentation, **PBMs face a gap between the clinical evidence required to make appropriate coverage decisions and the information accessible within existing workflows.** For Medicaid populations, where regulatory oversight and cost stewardship are especially important, this gap created friction for providers and risk for health plans working with the PBM. Administrative complexity in prior authorization processes has been[widely associated with increased provider burden and delays in treatment initiation,](https://www.ama-assn.org/press-center/ama-press-releases/ama-survey-indicates-prior-authorization-wreaks-havoc-patient-care) particularly for patients requiring specialty therapies.


## Understanding the PBM's challenges


Increasingly complex coverage criteria created several operational and clinical challenges:


- Prior authorizations required providers to call or fax supporting documentation
- Claims frequently rejected pending manual review
- Clinical staff manually validated coverage criteria
- Providers experienced delays in therapy initiation
- Plans risked inappropriate approvals or denials without full clinical context


## Our three-step approach


### A collaborative solution for improved coverage decisions


To address these challenges, the client and Labcorp collaborated on a three-step approach:


1.


#### Connecting clinical data to the point of adjudication:


The PBM implemented a real-time clinical data feed from Labcorp, enabling laboratory results to be available within pharmacy adjudication workflows rather than being requested after claim submission.


2.


#### Enabling automated clinical validation:


With lab data embedded into authorization logic, the PBM could evaluate coverage criteria using objective clinical evidence instead of manual documentation review. This allowed the organization to: evaluate clinical criteria automatically, confirm diagnoses using objective data and validate specialty eligibility without provider outreach


3.


#### Driving consistent and scalable decision making:


By integrating lab data into workflows, the PBM was able to apply coverage policies consistently while reducing administrative burden across the organization.


## Program impact


Healthcare coverage is shifting from documentation-based approval to evidence-based validation. As specialty therapies expand and regulations evolve, PBMs increasingly require objective clinical data to make timely coverage determinations.
